name: internetdata
description: Look up any IP address, AS or domain with InternetData: where an address is, whose network it's on, whether it's a VPN, a proxy, Tor or a hosting provider, a domain's DNS records and an AS's prefixes. Browse the InternetData databases and which ones your organization holds, too.

interface.shortDescription: Look up IPs, ASes and domains
interface.longDescription:
🔎 Look up any IP address, AS or domain and get the answer right in your chat.

🌍 What it answers
• Where an address is, whose network it's on and who uses it, with its abuse contact
• Whether it's a VPN, a residential, datacenter, mobile or public proxy, Tor, a privacy relay, a hosting provider or a CDN
• A domain's DNS records, its organization's IP ranges and whether it's a disposable email domain
• An AS's operator, its Whois record and the prefixes it announces

📋 Made for real work
• A whole list of addresses at once
• A signup or order export, with each answer kept next to its record
• The plan and allowance behind your API key
• The InternetData databases, and which ones your organization holds

🔒 Your key stays yours
• You sign in with your InternetData account and pick the API key it uses, and the key itself never reaches ChatGPT or Codex
• Every tool is read-only
• A field your plan doesn't include comes back marked as not covered, never as a no
defaultPrompt: Where is 8.8.8.8, and whose network is it on?
Is 185.220.101.1 a VPN, a proxy or Tor?
Does example.com have a mail server, and is it a disposable email domain?

positive.prompt: Where is 8.8.8.8, and whose network is it on?
positive.expected_behavior: Gives the address's country, its network and the company behind it, and reports a field the plan doesn't cover as not covered rather than as a no.

positive.description: Classify a list of addresses at once
positive.prompt: Check these addresses for VPNs, proxies and Tor: 45.83.91.1, 185.220.101.1, 8.8.8.8
positive.expected_behavior: Makes one call for the whole list and returns a row per address with its country, network and what it is (VPN, proxy, Tor, hosting or nothing found), flagged addresses first.

positive.prompt: Does example.com have a mail server, and is it a disposable email domain?
positive.expected_behavior: Says whether the domain is registered and has MX records, and reports the disposable flag, or says the key's plan doesn't cover it.

positive.description: List the databases and which ones the organization holds
positive.prompt: Which InternetData databases does my organization hold?
positive.expected_behavior: Lists each database family with its standing, licensed, expired or unlicensed, and marks the Open ones.

positive.prompt: What columns does the newest Tor IP database have? Show me a few sample rows.
positive.expected_behavior: Passes the versioned ID tor_ip_v1 and describes its columns and a few sample rows, saying the samples show the shape of the data and are not enough to count from.

negative.description: No tool downloads a database: the answer says the download happens in the console or with the InternetData CLI.
negative.prompt: Download the whole Tor IP database into this chat.

negative.description: Every tool is read-only, so the plugin cannot change an account or its keys.
The databases describe networks, not people, so the answer declines to identify anyone.
negative.prompt: Find the home address of whoever uses 203.0.113.7.

review.commerce_description: The plugin sells nothing. It reads what the API key the person picks at sign-in already has access to.

publication.release_notes: The listing's description reads in sections, each under a heading, with bullets. The tools and skills are the same as 1.0.5's.
